parsed.main_gap: The refinement lower bound falsely concludes the entire multigraph is a forest from having fewer edges than vertices; the chosen component may contain a cycle or loop.

errors.description: A graph with fewer edges than vertices can still contain a cyclic component alongside a tree or isolated component. Thus the component containing the arbitrarily designated vertex a_q need not be bipartite. The proof is readily repaired by observing that some component must be a tree and choosing that component instead.
errors.quote: Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on v vertices already uses at least v edges; hence every connected component C has e_C=v_C-1 and is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree). We use the component containing the vertex of a_q.

parsed.notes: Apart from this localized graph-theoretic error, the drafting lemma, refinement construction, subset-sum bound, and binary lower-bound strategy form a coherent and essentially complete proof.
